claim: Finite maximum-cardinality minimum-Euclidean-length bipartite matchings in general position are non-crossing.
remaining_gap: Does not ensure any stationary infinite-volume perfect limit.
checks: Strict triangle inequality; finite matching space; conditional algebra kernel-checked in FiniteChecks.lean.

claim: There exist stationary non-crossing partial matchings of the planar intensity-one Poisson inputs with total unmatched intensity E|Pois(L^2)-Pois(L^2)|/L^2 <= sqrt(2)/L, asymptotic to 2/(sqrt(pi)L).
remaining_gap: Matched displacements have not been proved uniformly tight as L grows.
checks: Full random-grid construction, stationarity proof, variance bound and characteristic-function/UI proof.

claim: F0082 has a positive answer iff stationary non-crossing partial matchings exist with unmatched intensity tending to zero and uniformly tight matched-displacement intensity.
remaining_gap: Existence of a sequence satisfying both properties is unproved.
checks: Vague compactness, endpoint isolation, proper-crossing stability and Poisson uniform integrability; explicit necessity proof.

claim: Perfect stationary non-crossing matchings can lose all edges under vague limits when tightness is omitted, for dependent shifted-lattice inputs.
remaining_gap: This is not a counterexample for independent Poisson inputs.
checks: Explicit irrational-slope parallel-segment example; exact proof of disjointness and escape.

claim: A unique bounded capped-length optimum, and a unique gamma=1/2 length-power optimum, can cross on four planar points.
remaining_gap: Only refutes automatic planarity of these cost objectives, not F0082.
checks: Exact inequalities; capped-cost experiment; rational distance certificates kernel-checked in FiniteChecks.lean.

claim: Finite rectangular Euclidean assignment experiments at side lengths 4,8,16,32 show no proper crossings among 1004164 checked pairs.
remaining_gap: Finite scales and floating point do not establish tightness or solve the infinite problem.
checks: Seed 82011, 16 replicates per size, all edge pairs in first two samples, costs from scipy.spatial.distance.cdist.

claim: Uniform displacement tightness for invariant gamma-minimal Poisson matchings as gamma approaches 1 from below would yield an invariant perfect 1-minimal planar matching.
remaining_gap: Uniform tightness has not been established.
checks: Joint compactness and passage of finite permutation inequalities through x^gamma continuity.

claim: There is no generic quasistability constant uniform for all gamma in (0,1) and all finite gamma-minimal configurations, even in planar general position.
remaining_gap: Does not rule out stochastic tightness for Poisson inputs.
checks: Exact four-point line construction, strict cost inequality near gamma=1, and continuity under small planar perturbations.

claim: Every continuous radial cost that weakly decreases under every proper red-blue uncrossing is affine At+B with A>=0; strict decrease requires A>0.
remaining_gap: Classifies an optimization mechanism, not existence of an invariant planar Poisson matching.
checks: Four-arm near-parallel limit in both orientations; full midpoint/dyadic proof; cost_probe.py; four-arm midpoint certificate kernel-checked in UncrossingCostChecks.lean (exit 0).

claim: Continuous displacement costs universally weakly compatible with uncrossing are exactly constant plus continuous sublinear functions; strict compatibility is strict subadditivity on independent vectors. Any coercive such cost dominates Euclidean length.
remaining_gap: Does not exclude explicitly crossing-constrained objectives or infinite-expected-cost constructions.
checks: Ray affinity, continuity at zero, exact epsilon crossing configuration, converse by triangle inequality, compact unit-circle minimum.

claim: No stationary planar nearly perfect Poisson matching family can have uniformly bounded expected coercive continuous universally-uncrossing-compatible additive displacement cost.
remaining_gap: Uniform tail tightness without a finite first moment remains possible and unproved.
checks: Linear domination, Markov tail bound, previously proved compactness criterion, compactly supported truncated length passage, source Theorem 2 infinite-mean obstruction.

claim: A stationary colour-aware partition into bounded convex cells with balanced counts and all points in cell interiors would produce a perfect stationary planar Poisson matching.
proof_location: SECOND_ATTEMPT.md Section C, sufficient construction target
remaining_gap: Such a genuinely two-dimensional colour-aware convex partition has not been constructed.
checks: Convex interiors, finite Euclidean minimizers, lexicographic equivariant selection.

claim: Independent equal-rate one-dimensional Poisson processes admit no stationary locally finite bi-infinite cuts avoiding input points with every consecutive interval count-balanced; consequently balanced bounded-rectangle partitions in stationary fixed-width strips are impossible.
proof_location: SECOND_ATTEMPT.md Section C, proposition and strip application
remaining_gap: Does not exclude general convex cells in the plane, nor arbitrary non-locally-finite planar strip matchings.
checks: Common signed-count level K, stationary coboundary K-K_t, uniform tail bound without moments, Skellam normal limit.

claim: A bounded-cell partition based solely on the uncoloured Poisson union and randomness independent of the colour marks cannot have every cell count-balanced.
remaining_gap: A successful colour-aware partition remains possible; this does not answer F0082.
checks: Conditional independent fair colours, balance probability <=1/2 in each finite nonempty cell, infinitely many disjoint cells.

claim: For continuous additive displacement cost C, existence of a non-crossing C-minimum matching for every finite balanced general-position input is equivalent to universal weak uncrossing, hence to C being constant plus continuous sublinear cost.
remaining_gap: Does not decide stationarity or perfectness for independent planar Poisson inputs.
checks: Finite primary-cost/secondary-length minimization; converse unique crossing two-edge optimum; exact squared-cost counterexample certified in Lean.
